title: The Premier League’s Winners and Losers From November International Break
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath6:00 PM ESTErling Haaland made sure that he enjoyed his time away from Manchester City. / Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesAnd we’re back. This fall may have felt like it has been composed of 90% international break at times, but that’s all behind us now, with no more club disruptions until March.
You can be forgiven for having taken your eye off the ball over the last two weeks with Premier League action on another hiatus.
As we reconvene ahead of the weekend, here’s a rundown of who benefitted most during the pause in action and who really didn’t.

The Gunners defense is about to get even stronger. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesIt’s a good time to be Arsenal. The Gunners went into the international break five points clear in the Premier League and return from it brimming with positive vibes.

A new contract has been typed up and is ready to receive Declan Rice’s signature, long-term absentee William Saliba is set to return to action after playing in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Watford and Ben White scored the winner for England against world champion Spain.
Even Viktor Gyökeres got a couple of goals against Bosnia and Herzegovina. All is well.
A very fond farewell. pic.twitter.com/vlru3E4cbp

Pochettino signed off his USMNT tenure in some style with an 8–0 aggregate win over Haiti, ensuring he delivered his adopted nation to the hallowed ground that is the Concacaf Nations League semifinal. He then immediately departed for Manchester on a lucrative two-and-half year deal.

There were hugs and tears all around as Pochettino made an emotional exit in Cincinnati. Named as Manchester United’s latest savior, and following a six-match winning run with the United States, his stock is as high as it has been since his Spurs days. There is no place that relishes taking managers down a peg quite like Old Trafford though.
In his first club interview with United, he promised to “love the players that we have and support them.” It’s a vow that might be tested once he gets to know them a bit better.
96th minute with a place in the quarter-finals on the line...Erling Haaland 🥶#NationsLeague pic.twitter.com/tclMdYwFeJ

Haaland put any Manchester City worries out of mind during the international break, scoring three times in two games against Wales and Denmark to help drag Norway kicking and screaming into the UEFA Nations League quarterfinal.
Norway’s goal monster now has 68 international strikes in just 61 outings, a rate of conversion that has seen him match the record of legendary Germany marksmen Gerd Müller in one fewer cap.
The Premier League’s leading goalscorer also extended his Nations League goals tally to 25, making him the all-time top scorer in the competition’s brief history.

Conor Bradley’s return is a welcome one. /  Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesThe Reds have been boosted by the return to training of long-term unavailable defensive pair Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni, who both suffered serious knee injuries last season.
Bradley, in particular, threatens to solve a standing issue at right back if he can get back up to speed in the near future—though loanee Ronald Araújo has shone as a makeshift option.
Elsewhere for Liverpool, Florian Wirtz reminded the world why he is a nine-figure soccer player, scoring twice and pulling every string in Germany’s 5–0 win over the Netherlands.
Jürgen Klopp claims to have “found the right position for Flo,” who also scored in his country’s 3–1 win over Serbia. Now, if he can just share that information with Liverpool.
